verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text: Dust on the windowsill spells out a name no one remembers now.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain finds the crack in the pavement it always finds,
patient as a habit no one asks about.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in an empty kitchen —
somewhere a door decides not to close all the way.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A child counts stairs out loud, losing the number each time —
the house keeps its own tally, patient as a heartbeat.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light hums against the moths' small storm —
someone inside has stopped waiting for morning.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A dog turns three times before lying down —
the whole yard settles when it finally does.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Steam rises off the road after rain —
the map in my pocket dissolves into directions I already knew.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it was ever silent —
this small rolling boil, a whole life deciding to speak.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's radio finds a station mid-song —
we hum the part we know, forgive ourselves the rest.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Porch light left on for no one in particular —
moths arrive anyway, believing in the invitation.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing, then stops —
satisfied the world has been warned.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone folds the map wrong on purpose —
a new country appears in the crease.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it's boiling, then remembers —
steam writes an apology on the cold window.

verses.text:
